--- title: "Visual attention span: symbols 3" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · HVIS_CAP_VAten_SIMBOLOS_3" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (F · Span and memory; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea HVIS_CAP_VAten_SIMBOLOS_3`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Amplitud visoatencional: símbolos 3*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/HVIS_CAP_VAten_SIMBOLOS_3.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Visual attention span: symbols 3, from age 5 to 6 (1,814 administrations in 2 cohorts). AUC .51–.53 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1915 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | brief visual presentation | | Items | — | | Task family | F · Span and memory | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | Primero aparecerá un asterisco para dirigir la atención al centro de la pantalla. Seguidamente, aparece una secuencia de 2 símbolos durante un tiempo tan breve que apenas se ve. *(Spanish)* | ## Theoretical framework **Visual-attentional span** is the number of visual elements processed simultaneously within a string. On the platform, a string of letters, numbers or symbols is briefly presented and the child chooses what they saw. **Serial search** asks whether there is an O among groups of Qs of different sizes. The **sustained attention** task (UNED battery) consists of 50 trials in which the child decides whether the name they hear matches the picture; despite its name, the catalog describes it as an index of inhibitory control. Reading requires processing several letters at once and maintaining attention along the line. **What the evidence says:** - **Visual-attentional span predicts reading beyond phonemic awareness.** In 417 French children in Grades 1, 3 and 5, it predicted reading independently of phonemic awareness, especially for irregular words [@bosse2009span]. Orthographic depth modulates how this attention is distributed: advanced bilinguals reading in French and Basque distributed it more evenly than those reading in Spanish and Basque [@antzaka2018depth]. - **Visual search is associated with reading, with small samples.** In 16 children with dyslexia and 16 controls, slow serial search was associated with visual-attentional span and with irregular word reading, not with phonology [@lallier2013search]. Visual scanning measured in preschool predicted learning to read in Italian children [@ferretti2008scanning]. - **Sustained attention is related more to comprehension than to word reading.** In 245 poor readers in Grades 4 and 5, it explained unique variance in comprehension, but not in reading accuracy or fluency [@macdonald2021sustained]. The evidence is weaker than for phonological processes and there are almost no studies in Spanish. **What our data show.** - **Letter and symbol subtests.** With 6–10 points and a single session, AUC from .47 to .61: separately they are not interpretable. - **Numbers and letters (36 items, ages 4–5).** α = .60 and AUC of .66–.67 against persistent difficulty and of .65 against later low comprehension. It is the best in the family, as expected of alphanumeric stimuli. - **Numbers (16 items).** α = .56 and almost zero stability across school years (ρ = .05–.19). AUC from .54 to .69. - **Serial search.** α = .74, ceiling of 11–20% and AUC from .58 to .63. - **Sustained attention.** Despite an α of .95, it shows no validity: extreme ceiling (median 45 out of 50), stability of ρ = .03–.16, null correlation with the other domains and AUC from .43 to .56. It should not be used until the data have been reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 5.1| 2011| 153|2016/17 | 898| 0| 898| 34| | 6.1| 2010| 152|2016/17 | 916| 263| 652| 34| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 6.1| 263| 2010| 2.13| 1.21| 2| 0.29| 7.98| 3.80| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 6.1| 263|0–5 |0–5 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (5.1, r = .06); Phonological awareness (6.1, r = .12). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .51–.53. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .47–.54. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HVIS_CAP_VAten_SIMBOLOS_3_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .51–.60 (2 time points; 260–266 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 5.1| 898| 2011| 0| 1| 1| 1| 2| 3| 4| | 6.1| 263| 2010| 0| 1| 1| 1| 2| 3| 4| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HVIS_CAP_VAten_SIMBOLOS_3_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 5.1| 898| 0.011| 0.752| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.1| 894| 0.045| 0.513| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.1| 889| -0.054| 0.109| |School (ICC) | 5.1| 898| 0.050| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.1| 916| 0.072| 0.030| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.1| 914| 0.094| 0.160| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.1| 913| 0.043| 0.190| |School (ICC) | 6.1| 916| 0.019| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Visual attention span: symbols 3” (code 1915; LEEDUCA battery) assesses visual attention span. A string of visual stimuli is briefly presented and the child reports those seen. The time limit is 20 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010 and 2011 cohorts it was administered in 2 sessions, from 5 to 6 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .47–.54. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
